items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: INTERVIEWER: What's that young boy, Sir Charles somebody?

ctx.x: That's an awful feeling. So, they was working at a place called Club Sudan (phonetic). I was in the relief band. I was up there singing the blues and I had a little short trumpet up there and we was swinging pretty good too.
They had some beautiful musicians -- they had Fats up there, they had Dizzy, they had everybody who was anybody. What's that young boy, Sir Charles somebody?

items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Okay, also now, Mingus one on it... But, you know, Ellington wrote that, it wasn't Jimmy Forrest.

ctx.x: Okay, also now, Mingus one on it (humming). Then he repeats, and then he's got a bridge that he puts on it. But, you know, Ellington wrote that, it wasn't Jimmy Forrest.
